entries.title: Psalms 107:1
segments: The theme of this psalm is God's goodness in delivering the afflicted of various classes.  It may have special reference to the restoration of God's people from captivity; but is manifestly designed for general application.

entries.title: Psalms 107:2
segments: All deliverances should be acknowledged with devout thanksgiving; but they whom the Lord has redeemed from sin and death eternal, have the most abundant cause to bless him for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men.

entries.title: Psalms 107:3
segments: Gathered them; from the lands in which they had been dispersed on account of their sins.

entries.title: Psalms 107:10
segments:
Darkness and--shadow of death; imprisoned in dark dungeons. 
 
  Bound in affliction and iron; afflicted by being bound in iron fetters; referring to men whom God has given over to imprisonment as a chastisement for their sins.

entries.title: Psalms 107:11
segments: Sin is the cause of all the troubles with which men are afflicted, and their deliverance from it is often designed by Jehovah in bringing calamities upon them.

entries.title: Psalms 107:12
segments: Labor; the original word denotes sorrowful toil.

entries.title: Psalms 107:16
segments: No calamities of men in this life are so great that the Lord cannot deliver them, even should they be like those of Manasseh in chains, or Daniel in the dungeon, or Jonah in the whale's belly.

entries.title: Psalms 107:17
segments:
Fools; in the scriptural sense;  that is, transgressors of God's law. 
 
  Are afflicted; with sickness,
.  The holy Scriptures regarded sickness as well as all other suffering, as the fruit of sin.

entries.title: Psalms 107:22
segments: The blessings which God bestows should be acknowledged with devout thanksgiving, and bind the soul in sweet and hearty obedience to his service.

entries.title: Psalms 107:28
segments: The deliverance of seamen and such as do business on the sea, should inspire them especially with a conviction of the goodness of God, their dependence on him, and their obligations to love and obey him.

entries.title: Psalms 107:30
segments: Men may be glad without being grateful, and rejoice in the gift without giving glory to the Giver.

entries.title: Psalms 107:33
segments: Turneth rivers into a wilderness; the psalm closes with God's providential dealings with nations.

entries.title: Psalms 107:35
segments: National, not less than individual prosperity depends upon God's blessing, which will rest only upon the people who acknowledge his supremacy and obey his word.

entries.title: Psalms 107:38
segments: The increase of worldly substance and of the comfort derived from it is of the Lord, an lays the possessor under increasing obligations to learn and do his will.

entries.title: Psalms 107:43
segments:
These things; the course of God's providence. 
 
  The loving-kindness of the Lord; towards those who truly repent of sin, and seek him with the whole heart. 
 
A careful attention to the dealings of God with men will show his loving kindness and tender mercy to all who put their trust in him.
